title: Successful user registration with valid data
description: Verifies successful creation of a new user account when all registration data meets field validation rules and triggers the email verification workflow.
testDescription: As a new user, I want to register for an account by submitting a registration form with valid data so that my account is created and I receive a verification email as confirmation.
prerequisites: No existing account with the provided email address. Test environment is configured to send emails. All mandatory fields are known and ready for input.
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the registration page in the web portal.
2. Enter a valid first_name (minimum 2, maximum 50 alpha characters; e.g., 'Alice').
3. Enter a valid last_name (minimum 2, maximum 50 alpha characters; e.g., 'Smith').
4. Enter a unique, valid RFC 5322 formatted email (e.g., 'alice.smith1990@example.com').
5. Enter a strong password that meets the requirements (minimum 12 chars; at least 1 uppercase, 1 lowercase, 1 digit, 1 symbol; e.g., 'Secure@Passw0rd1').
6. Enter a date_of_birth such that the user is exactly 18 years old or older (e.g., '2000-03-10').
7. Enter a valid phone_number in E.164 format (e.g., '+14165551234').
8. Enter a valid ssn_last4 (exactly 4 numeric digits; e.g., '8421').
9. Set agree_terms to true, confirming agreement to terms and conditions.
10. Submit the registration form.
11. Wait for the API response and capture the HTTP status code and body.
12. Verify that a verification email is received at the registered address.
13. Confirm that the response includes 'user_id' and 'verification_token'.
expectedResult: API returns HTTP 201 with user_id and verification_token in the response; a verification email is sent to the user's email address.

sourceCitation.excerpt: POST/v2/auth/register... Triggers email verification workflow. Field NameTypeRequiredValidation Rule... first_nameStringRequiredMin 2 chars,max 50 chars,alpha only

title: Successful token refresh after expiry
description: Verifies that a user can obtain a new access token by submitting a valid refresh token after access token expiry, and that token rotation is enforced.
testDescription: As an authenticated user, when my access token expires, I can exchange a valid, unused refresh token for a new access and refresh token pair so I can continue using the service.

stepsToPerform:
1. Login as a valid user and acquire access_token and refresh_token.
2. Wait until the access_token has expired (simulate token expiry or advance system time as needed).
3. Prepare POST /v2/auth/token/refresh with the valid refresh_token in the request body.
4. Submit the refresh request.
5. Capture the API HTTP status code and response body.
6. Extract access_token and refresh_token fields from the response.
7. Attempt to use the new access_token for a protected resource to confirm its validity.
8. Attempt to reuse the previously used refresh_token and record the response (for completeness).
expectedResult: API returns HTTP 200 with new access_token and refresh_token; the previous refresh_token is invalidated and cannot be reused.

sourceCitation.excerpt: POST/v2/auth/token/refresh... Issues a new access token... rotation enforced.

testDescription: As a logged-in user on the web portal, if I remain inactive for 15 minutes, my session should expire, requiring re-authentication for further access.

testDescription: A user accesses card detail screens and payment forms. The test inspects browser UI and DOM to confirm that only masked PAN (**** **** **** 1234) is rendered and that card entry fields utilize iframe tokenisation (Stripe Elements). No full PAN is transmitted or stored on frontend. TLS 1.3 is confirmed in transport layer.
prerequisites: Active card exists with PAN ending in 1234. User authenticated. Browser dev tools ready for DOM inspection. Network supports TLS 1.3. Payment form is accessible.
stepsToPerform:
1. Log in as user with valid JWT.
2. Navigate to card detail screen on web portal.
3. Inspect displayed PAN format; confirm it is masked (**** **** **** 1234).
4. Open browser dev tools and check DOM for PAN presence.
5. Confirm no full PAN anywhere in DOM.
6. Initiate payment form; examine card input fields.
7. Verify fields are embedded via iframe tokenisation (e.g., Stripe Elements, no direct input).
8. Use network analyzer to confirm TLS 1.3 is used in all transmissions.
9. Attempt to copy or extract full PAN from field or network: confirm cannot.
10. Validate no full PAN is stored or cached client-side.
expectedResult: Only masked PAN (**** **** **** 1234) displayed UI-side. No full PAN present in DOM or JavaScript. Card fields are iframe tokenised. All network transmissions over TLS 1.3.

sourceCitation.excerpt: PAN displayed in browser as **** **** **** 1234 only. Full PAN never transmitted to frontend. Card fields use iframe tokenisation... TLS 1.3.

title: No raw PAN in DOM and audit coverage for PCI-DSS
description: Validates that no full PAN data is ever present in the browser DOM and that card input fields use secure, PCI-compliant iframe tokenisation.
testDescription: Inspect all web portal screens, especially payment forms, to ensure no raw PAN is injected, present, or accessible anywhere in DOM. All input fields for card numbers must be served via PCI-compliant iframe (e.g., Stripe Elements).
prerequisites: User authenticated. Card products active. Payment and card entry forms accessible. Browser dev tools ready for audit.
stepsToPerform:
1. Log in as account holder with valid JWT.
2. Access all card-related forms and screens.
3. Open dev tools and review DOM for full PAN presence.
4. Confirm that card input fields are loaded within iframes.
5. Validate fields do not allow direct DOM access to PAN.
6. Review any browser storage, JavaScript objects, or caches for card number content.
7. Submit card details on a payment form.
8. Monitor DOM for any dynamic injection or leaks of PAN.
9. Audit DOM snapshot for compliance, confirming no raw PAN.
10. Document and report any PCI-DSS violations.
expectedResult: No raw PAN found anywhere in DOM, JavaScript, or browser storage. All card fields are iframe tokenised. PCI-DSS audit log shows no exposure.

sourceCitation.excerpt: No raw PAN in DOM. Card fields use iframe tokenisation (Stripe Elements or equivalent).

title: CSRF token required for state-changing endpoints
description: Validates that all state-changing API endpoints enforce CSRF token requirement in X-CSRF-Token header.
testDescription: Submit PATCH and POST requests to state-changing endpoints (e.g., /v2/cards/{card_id}/status, /v2/accounts/{account_id}/payments) both with and without the X-CSRF-Token header. Confirm that requests without the header are rejected per compliance.
prerequisites: User is authenticated with valid JWT. State-changing endpoints accessible. Known valid X-CSRF-Token available for session.
stepsToPerform:
1. Log in and obtain JWT plus valid CSRF token from session.
2. Attempt PATCH /v2/cards/{card_id}/status with valid X-CSRF-Token.
3. Confirm status update is successful.
4. Repeat PATCH request without X-CSRF-Token header.
5. Observe error response for missing token.
6. Attempt POST /v2/accounts/{account_id}/payments with valid X-CSRF-Token.
7. Confirm payment is accepted.
8. Resubmit payment request without X-CSRF-Token.
9. Observe error response for missing token.
10. Confirm all state-changing endpoints enforce token protection.
expectedResult: State-changing requests succeed only when X-CSRF-Token is present. Missing header results in compliance rejection.

sourceCitation.excerpt: All state-changing endpoints require a CSRF token in X-CSRF-Token header.

title: SameSite=Strict cookie policy enforced
description: Validates that all session cookies used by the portal are set with SameSite=Strict attribute to mitigate CSRF risks.
testDescription: Inspect session cookies generated during authentication and throughout portal interaction. Confirm all cookies related to authentication and session state are set and transmitted with SameSite=Strict. Attempt cross-site requests and observe cookie refusal.
prerequisites: User is authenticated. Portal uses cookie-based session storage. Browser dev tools available for inspect.
stepsToPerform:
1. Log in as user and complete authentication flow.
2. Open browser dev tools and review cookie attributes.
3. Confirm SameSite=Strict flag is set for all session-identifying cookies.
4. Attempt to access portal from cross-site iframe or embedded frame.
5. Observe cookie transmission behavior.
6. Execute API requests from an external origin and check for cookie refusal.
7. Validate session cookie is not transmitted cross-site.
8. Complete authenticated actions and observe cookie integrity.
9. Attempt to inject cookies from cross-origin script and confirm failure.
10. Document compliance for CSRF mitigation.
expectedResult: All session cookies are set SameSite=Strict. No authenticated cookies are sent cross-site. CSRF attack surface is minimized.

sourceCitation.excerpt: SameSite=Strict cookie policy enforced.

title: Audit trail logs for credit_limit changes
description: Ensures that every credit_limit change triggers an audit log entry including user_id, session_id, ip_address, timestamp_utc, and that audit trail is immutable and retrievable.
testDescription: Change the credit_limit for an account, then retrieve audit logs and confirm that an entry is recorded for the event, capturing user_id, session_id, ip_address, timestamp_utc. Attempt to modify or delete audit entries to verify immutability.
prerequisites: Account exists. Admin or compliance user role enabled. Audit retrieval endpoint accessible.
stepsToPerform:
1. Log in as admin/compliance user.
2. Change credit_limit for a selected account via PATCH /v2/accounts/{account_id}/credit-limit.
3. Wait for change confirmation.
4. Access audit trail retrieval API and fetch latest audit entries.
5. Confirm entry for credit_limit change is present.
6. Review entry fields for user_id, session_id, ip_address, timestamp_utc.
7. Attempt to edit or delete audit entry and confirm operation is forbidden.
8. Validate audit entry is retrievable at any time.
9. Cross-verify audit log with event timestamp.
10. Document audit trail completeness.
expectedResult: Audit entry exists including user_id, session_id, ip_address, timestamp_utc. Entry is immutable and retrievable. Attempted modifications are rejected.

sourceCitation.excerpt: All credit_limit changes log user_id, session_id, ip_address, timestamp_utc to immutable audit log.

title: Audit logging for card status changes and events
description: Validates that card status changes (e.g., freeze/unfreeze/lost/stolen) log a 255-char max reasonString to the audit trail, and are retrievable with required fields.
testDescription: Freeze and unfreeze a card, then report it lost, each with a unique reasonString. Retrieve audit trail and confirm events are logged with correct reason, timestamp, and event type as per requirements.
prerequisites: Card is active and belongs to authenticated user. Audit retrieval API enabled. User can provide unique reasonString per event.
stepsToPerform:
1. Log in as cardholder with valid JWT.
2. Freeze card via PATCH /v2/cards/{card_id}/status with confirm_otp and reasonString ('Travel security').
3. Unfreeze card via PATCH with reasonString ('Return from trip').
4. Report card lost via POST /v2/cards/{card_id}/report-lost with reasonString ('Left in taxi').
5. Retrieve audit trail for card events.
6. Confirm each event is logged with reasonString, event type, timestamp.
7. Verify reasonString is truncated at 255 chars if longer.
8. Validate fields: reasonString, event type, timestamp, card_id.
9. Attempt to delete or modify audit event and confirm it is forbidden.
10. Document audit completeness for card events.
expectedResult: Each card status change or loss event is logged to audit trail with reasonString (max 255 chars), event type, timestamp, and card_id. Events are immutable and retrievable.

title: API p95 latency ≤ 1500 ms under load
description: Verifies that 95th percentile (p95) API response latency does not exceed 1,500 ms when subjected to sustained load according to scalability requirements.
testDescription: As a performance tester, I want to validate that the API consistently delivers responses under 1,500 ms at the 95th percentile when exposed to realistic web traffic loads. This ensures the portal meets latency SLAs for end users per NFR requirements.
prerequisites: System deployed to performance environment with production-like hardware, WAF/rate-limiters active. No other tests stressing shared infra. Tools such as JMeter or Locust available. All API endpoints are healthy.
stepsToPerform:
1. Choose a representative production GET endpoint, e.g., /v2/accounts/{account_id}/summary.
2. Configure test runner with unique, valid authentication tokens for all concurrent sessions.
3. Set up a load profile: ramp up to 3,000 requests per second over 5 minutes, maintain for 10 minutes.
4. Randomize account_id parameters from pre-loaded test data, re-using tokens where realistic.
5. Ensure all requests include valid headers (Authorization, CSRF where required).
6. Begin the 10-minute sustained load, capturing per-request timestamps, status, and response latency.
7. After test completion, aggregate total requests, success/failure rates, and compute latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99).
8. Isolate latency measurements by HTTP 200 responses only (other codes excluded).
9. Review infrastructure logs for rate limit or error spikes during the load period.
10. Document the highest p95 latency captured.
expectedResult: API p95 response latency measured does not exceed 1,500 ms for all tested endpoints at 3,000 RPS (request per second) sustained. No more than 1% errors. All HTTP 200 responses at or under 1,500 ms p95.

sourceCitation.excerpt: NFR-02LatencyAPI p95 latency ≤ 1,500 ms.

title: API gateway sustains 5,000 concurrent requests/sec
description: Verifies that the API gateway can handle at least 5,000 concurrent requests per second and enforces appropriate scaling, per system scalability requirements.
testDescription: As a system tester, I want to confirm the API gateway's ability to handle 5,000 simultaneous requests per second with no degradation in service, and verify that auto-scaling triggers if CPU usage exceeds 70%.
prerequisites: Staging/performance environment must allow traffic up to documented thresholds. Auto-scaling must be configured and monitored. Valid test accounts with necessary data exist.
stepsToPerform:
1. Set up and verify cloud monitoring for CPU utilization and auto-scaling group status.
2. Prepare a pool of 5,000 test users/accounts with valid JWT tokens.
3. Configure a load testing tool to simulate 5,000 concurrent requests/sec to a representative endpoint (/v2/accounts/{account_id}/summary).
4. Each request uses a different account_id/token, randomized per run.
5. Include valid Authorization and CSRF headers for all requests.
6. Ramp up load to 5,000 RPS in increments over 5 minutes, then maintain for at least 10 minutes.
7. Measure and log HTTP success/error rates and latency metrics throughout the test window.
8. During the test, monitor CPU utilization on the API gateway node(s).
9. Take note if CPU utilization crosses 70%, and observe auto-scaling behaviors (new instances/containers added).
10. After load, verify the system returns to baseline state and no errors persist.
expectedResult: API gateway services all 5,000 concurrent requests/sec with sustained throughput; error rate does not exceed 1%. If CPU utilization reaches or exceeds 70%, auto-scaling is triggered and additional nodes are provisioned as per requirement.

sourceCitation.excerpt: API gateway must sustain 5,000 concurrent requests/sec. Auto-scaling triggers at 70% CPU utilisation.

title: Notification webhook delivers LATE_PAYMENT alert to all channels
description: Verifies that a valid LATE_PAYMENT alert is dispatched via the notification webhook to all supported channels (EMAIL, PUSH, IN_APP, SMS), with required payload fields and successful delivery.
testDescription: As a business process owner, I want to ensure that submitting a LATE_PAYMENT notification via the webhook triggers alert delivery to all user channels, meeting requirements for regulatory communication and user awareness.
prerequisites: A test account (account_id) exists with all notification channels (EMAIL, PUSH, IN_APP, SMS) enabled for the user. Proper test webhooks exist for each channel. Notification Engine and webhook endpoints are reachable.
stepsToPerform:
1. For the test account, confirm all four notification channels are enabled and configured.
2. Generate a unique idempotency_key (UUID v4) for the LATE_PAYMENT alert.
3. Compose a valid POST payload to /v2/notifications/webhook with fields: account_id, alert_type=LATE_PAYMENT, channel=EMAIL, message_body, severity=WARNING, idempotency_key.
4. Send the payload for EMAIL channel; log response.
5. Repeat steps 3-4, updating the channel to PUSH; send and log responses.
6. Repeat for IN_APP and SMS channels, reusing the same idempotency_key value.
7. For each POST, verify HTTP 200 and presence of notification_id, delivered_at, channel in the response.
8. Confirm delivery/appearance of alerts in the target system (e.g., received email, mobile push, in-app banner, SMS) for each channel.
9. Check audit/log system for delivery status for all four notifications.
expectedResult: All four alert channels (EMAIL, PUSH, IN_APP, SMS) receive the LATE_PAYMENT alert for the test account; API responds with HTTP 200 and notification_id per channel. Each channel’s delivery is confirmed via appropriate mechanism, as per payload.

title: Idempotency key prevents duplicate notifications
description: Verifies the notification webhook's use of idempotency_key to prevent duplicate alert delivery. Duplicate submissions must return a 409 error with the specified error body.
testDescription: As a compliance tester, I want to ensure that submitting the same notification payload with an identical idempotency_key twice does not result in duplicate alert deliveries, and the API responds with the documented error.
prerequisites: Notification Engine and webhook are online. The target account/channel is ready and able to receive alerts. No conflicting ids in system for test period.
stepsToPerform:
1. Generate a unique UUID v4 idempotency_key for this test.
2. Prepare a valid POST /v2/notifications/webhook payload with: account_id, alert_type=FRAUD_FLAG, channel=EMAIL, message_body, severity=CRITICAL, idempotency_key.
3. Send the first notification POST request; check HTTP 200 response and receipt of notification_id.
4. Retry the identical POST (no changes to payload or idempotency_key) within 1 minute.
5. Capture the HTTP response; verify it is HTTP 409.
6. Inspect error response body for 'error: DUPLICATE_NOTIFICATION'.
7. Check backend logs (if accessible) to confirm only one alert was processed/delivered.
8. Repeat steps 2-7 for another alert_type (e.g., STATEMENT_READY) to demonstrate generality.
9. Optionally, retry with altered idempotency_key should succeed and return HTTP 200.
expectedResult: First submission triggers one notification and returns HTTP 200. Exact duplicate (same idempotency_key) triggers a 409 with error: DUPLICATE_NOTIFICATION, and no second alert is delivered.

title: Notification error handling for unknown alert type

testDescription: As a security and stability tester, I want to send a POST /v2/notifications/webhook with an invalid alert_type to verify the system rejects the request with HTTP 400 and the documented error details.

2. Select a valid channel (e.g., EMAIL) and generate unique idempotency_key (UUID v4).
3. Construct webhook payload with alert_type=INVALID_TYPE (not in allowed enums), valid channel, message_body, severity=INFO, idempotency_key.

title: Right to rescind: delete account within 14 days, no fee
description: Verifies that the DELETE account endpoint allows account closure within the allowed 14-day window post-issuance, and confirms no membership fee is present. Attempts after 14 days are rejected.
testDescription: As a regulatory QA engineer, I want to ensure users can delete their credit card account within 14 days of issuance via DELETE /v2/accounts/{id} without incurring a membership fee, and any requests after 14 days are rejected as per requirement REQ-016.
prerequisites: A test user account with fresh card issuance (<14 days since creation). Endpoint is unblocked; membership fee not charged yet. Secondary account ≥15 days old for negative variation.
stepsToPerform:
1. Record the creation date (issuance timestamp) for the test account.
2. Ensure current date/time is within 14 days of issuance.
3. With valid authentication, send a DELETE request to /v2/accounts/{id} for this test account.
4. Confirm API requires and processes Authorization and CSRF tokens.
5. Capture HTTP response; verify HTTP 200 or 204 indicating successful deletion.
6. Verify in account summary that account is now inactive/closed and no membership fee has been charged (verify transaction history and balance).
7. Attempt to access the account dashboard with old credentials; expect failure/forbidden (account does not exist or is closed).
8. Attempt to delete an account aged >14 days; capture the response.
9. Verify this second response is not 200, has explicit error indicating account closure window expired (as per source; error wording if present).
10. Check for side effects: other products, records, audit trail for deletion event.
expectedResult: Account deleted successfully if request made within 14 days post-issuance, with no membership fee transaction present. Deletion attempted after 14 days is rejected by the endpoint. Account becomes inaccessible after deletion.

sourceCitation.excerpt: DELETE /v2/accounts/{{id}} must be available for 14 days post-issuance with no membership fee. Endpoint rejects after Day 14.
